I S. 1822), as amended; German Transparency Register and Financial Information Act (Transparenzregister- und Finanzinformationsgesetz – TraFinG) implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 establishing the EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA); §20 GwG requires mandatory disclosure of beneficial owners to the Transparency Register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil registry authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-country competent authority if the Hague Convention applies; otherwise consular legalization at the German embassy or consulate in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or corporate registry competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the German Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) sanctions list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Sanctions List, and the German Bundesanzeiger sanctions-related publications; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is obligatory for PEPs under GwG §1(12) and §7; additional provenance checks required for high-risk third-country jurisdictions related to herbal botanical supply chains.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.industry_license_detail: A food business notification under Article 65 of EU Regulation 2017/625 and national LI Lebensmittelüberwachungs- und -Verbraucherinfoportalgesetz; a wholesaler of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals must register with the local competent district food-safety authority (Lebensmittelüberwachungsamt) before commencing operations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.payment_rails_aml_notes: Incoming Swift TT and wire transfers require bank-side beneficiary verification, specified-payer-name validation under EU Regulation 2015/847, and enhanced due diligence on recurring counterparties in non-EU jurisdictions.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.country_specific_sourcing_banned_token: Goji berries sourced from any country subject to EU autonomous trade restrictions are not permitted; all imports must comply with EU phytosanitary and pesticide residue standards under Regulation (EC) 396/2005.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Unternehmensregister/Handelsregister – official electronic registry at www.handelsregister.de and www.unternehmensregister.de
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in the Latin alphabet using German script; the legal form suffix must appear as 'Unternehmergesellschaft (haftungsbeschränkt)' or 'UG (haftungsbeschränkt)'; non-German words are permitted if transliterated into Latin characters and not misleading; the name must be distinguishable within the corporate registry and must not deceive consumers regarding the scope or legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the local Amtsgericht, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the same Amtsgericht within one month after receipt of the negative notice; the appeal can be prepared and submitted through a licensed German notary; if the rejection is based on identity confusion with a prior registered mark, the applicant may withdraw and reapply with a modified name or file for a parallel civil hearing under the German Code of Civil Procedure (ZPO §§54–63). Further judicial review is available through the Higher Regional Court (Landgericht) in the registry district.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.special_hook_geo_token: No additional special-token override; the standard German registry practice applies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without physical business presence is impermissible as the sole registered seat of a UG engaging in wholesale export of physical goods; a serviced office or coworking meeting address is accepted only where it allows genuine mail receipt, business records access, and management presence; any address arrangement must be disclosed to the commercial register and not function as an anonymizing shell.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium 5_To_15_Percent_Annual_Risk – Federal and municipal authorities may conduct unannounced inspections, particularly in connection with food import controls, tax registration verification, and anti-money-laundering compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.substantive_requirements: The UG must maintain complete accounting records, food-safety logbooks, and underlying procurement documents at the registered office so that they are available for immediate physical inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_override: Allowed only as an additional correspondence address; statutory seat must remain a physical German address controlled by the managing director.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.nominee_directorial_override: No nominee director arrangement is permitted in Germany; the managing director must be a natural person able to produce a valid ID and accept personal entrepreneurial liability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: German Limited Liability Companies Act (GmbHG), Sections 1, 5a, 7, 8, 10, 35, 39, 46, 78; Commercial Code (HGB) Sections 8-16
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Amtsgericht (Court of First Instance) – Commercial Register Department (Handelsregisterabteilung)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) and Application for Registration (Anmeldung) to the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital EUR 1.00 (fully paid in cash before registration); no escrow account required, but capital must be credited to a German bank account in the company's name; UG must retain 25% of annual net profits until share capital reaches EUR 25,000
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the company adopts the Articles of Association as presented and subscribes to the initial share capital of EUR 1.00, fully paid in cash. (2) That the registered office of the company is established at [Street, City, Germany]. (3) That [Name] is appointed as Managing Director (Geschäftsführer) with sole representation authority, and [Name] as Deputy Managing Director. (4) That the Managing Director is authorized to execute all filings with the Commercial Register, tax authorities, and trade office. (5) That the company's fiscal year commences on the date of registration. (6) That the Managing Director shall open a corporate bank account and deposit the share capital. (7) That all actions taken prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notar) in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to draft the Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) in German, including company name, registered office, object (wholesale trade of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals), share capital (EUR 1.00), and management provisions. All founders must appear before the notary to sign. The notary will verify identity and certify the document.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (lease agreement or landlord consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the draft and resubmit. If founders are non-residents, provide apostilled and translated documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank (e.g., Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank) or online bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name (pre-registration account). Deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 1.00. Obtain a confirmation of deposit (Sperrvermerk) from the bank, which is required for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional due diligence, provide beneficial ownership declaration and business plan. If the account is rejected, use a different bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Registration with Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized application (Anmeldung) to the Commercial Register, including the Articles of Association, list of managing directors, and bank confirmation. The notary typically files electronically. The court reviews compliance with GmbHG and HGB.
required_dossiers: List of managing directors with signatures
Proof of trade license (if already obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query, respond within 2 weeks with clarifications or amended documents. If the application is rejected, correct the deficiencies and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Commercial Register Extract and Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the court issues a registration certificate (Handelsregisterauszug) and publishes the registration in the electronic Federal Gazette (Bundesanzeiger). The company becomes legally effective on the date of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extract contains errors, request correction from the court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Purposes with Local Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Finanzamt (Tax Office) responsible for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) electronically via ELSTER portal. Provide details of business activities, expected turnover, and bank account. The tax office will issue a tax number (Steuernummer) and VAT number (USt-IdNr.) if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, respond promptly. If the questionnaire is incomplete, correct and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Trade License (Gewerbeschein) from Local Trade Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Gewerbeamt (Trade Office) of the city or municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) with the local trade office, indicating the business activity (wholesale of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals). The trade office will issue a trade license (Gewerbeschein) after checking for any disqualifications. This license is required for all commercial activities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of no criminal record (Führungszeugnis) for managing director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the trade office raises objections, provide additional documentation or appeal. If the license is denied, consult a lawyer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Trade Office (Gewerbeamt) and Federal Office for Agriculture and Food (BLE) for export certificates
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trade License (Gewerbeschein) and Export Certificate for Food Products (if applicable)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt) and local environmental authority (Untere Umweltschutzbehörde)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Trading activity with no manufacturing or significant emissions; only registration under the Federal Immission Control Act (BImSchG) if storage exceeds thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge or VOC emissions from trading operations. If warehousing is involved, comply with storage regulations for food products (hygiene standards per EU Regulation 852/2004). Waste handling must follow the Closed Substance Cycle and Waste Management Act (KrWG).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire department (Brandschutz) for any storage facility; structural load inspection for warehouses; occupational health and safety clearance per the Occupational Safety Act (ArbSchG) and Workplace Ordinance (ArbStättV).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal tax administration: Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt), including its online services for VAT identification numbers and EU VAT procedures; the competent local Finanzamt administers domestic tax registration and tax numbers. ELSTER is the principal electronic tax filing and registration platform. Customs matters are administered by the Generalzolldirektion and the relevant Hauptzollamt.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A German UG must submit the electronic Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung through ELSTER to the Finanzamt competent for its registered office, generally within one month after commencing business activity. The Finanzamt issues the domestic Steuernummer and assesses corporate income tax, trade tax, and VAT registration. Apply separately to the BZSt for a VAT identification number (USt-IdNr.), normally after or in connection with tax registration; an EU-established business may also apply through its competent tax office. A foreign-established taxable person without a German establishment applies to the Finanzamt designated for its country of establishment and provides incorporation documents, proof of business activity, address and representative details, and any requested evidence of taxable transactions. A non-EU business may be required to appoint a fiscal representative for specified VAT arrangements; representation does not replace the taxable person's liability. Obtain an EORI number from German customs before relevant customs operations. A German UG is not a foreign entity and follows the domestic registration route.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Germany has no US-style check-the-box election for a UG. A UG is a separate corporate income tax taxpayer and is generally subject to trade tax. Under section 1a KStG, eligible commercial partnerships may elect corporate income tax treatment, subject to statutory conditions; that election is not a pass-through election available to a UG. German domestic and treaty rules determine entity characterization for cross-border purposes. Anti-hybrid rules, including section 4k EStG and related provisions, can deny deductions or impose other consequences for mismatches; they are not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold exempts a German-established UG from VAT registration and compliance where it makes taxable supplies. The small-business regime under section 19 UStG may apply if prior-year total turnover does not exceed EUR 25,000 and current-year total turnover does not exceed EUR 100,000; it is an exemption regime, not a general registration threshold, and has statutory exclusions. A foreign-established supplier making taxable supplies in Germany generally has no domestic registration threshold. Separate EU small-enterprise rules may apply to qualifying cross-border EU supplies subject to their conditions and turnover limits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Germany has no general real-time VAT clearance, government digital-stamping, or mandatory pre-approval system for invoices. From 1 January 2025, domestic businesses must be able to receive structured electronic invoices for domestic B2B transactions. The obligation to issue structured e-invoices is being phased in: transitional permission to issue other invoices generally applies through 2026, with a further transition through 2027 for specified suppliers with prior-year turnover not exceeding EUR 800,000. From 2028, structured e-invoicing is generally required for in-scope domestic B2B transactions, subject to statutory exceptions. A qualifying e-invoice must use a compliant structured format, such as EN 16931 or an accepted equivalent; ordinary PDF invoices alone are not structured e-invoices. Invoicing and VAT records must be retained in accordance with German law and GoBD principles.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods may be exempt with credit (zero-rated) under sections 4 no. 1(a) and 6 UStG where the statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains prescribed evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The applicable evidence depends on whether the export is made by the supplier or by the non-EU customer. An intra-Community supply is treated under separate rules and requires, among other conditions, dispatch to another EU Member State, a qualifying business customer and valid VAT identification details, plus evidence and reporting compliance. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or payment is offshore: place-of-supply rules govern, and a service may be outside German VAT or exempt only where a specific rule applies. Input VAT recovery is subject to the ordinary deduction rules and substantiation requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and export accompanying or exit confirmation evidence, including the electronic Ausgangsvermerk where available
Commercial invoice, order or contract, and records identifying the goods, quantity, purchaser, and shipment
Transport evidence appropriate to the transaction, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or carrier documentation; a bill of lading is not universally required
Proof of delivery or other evidence of departure from the EU customs territory where required under the applicable evidence rules
Evidence of payment or inward remittance may support the audit trail but is not a universal statutory condition for export zero-rating
For intra-Community supplies, customer VAT identification evidence, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Germany imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The supplier must substantiate the conditions for exemption and maintain compliant VAT records. If evidence is missing or the conditions are not met, the tax authority may assess German VAT, interest under the applicable rules, and related procedural charges. Intentional or reckless tax evasion may result in criminal or administrative penalties under the Abgabenordnung; inaccurate returns may also attract tax surcharges. Input VAT refunds or credits may be denied or reclaimed, with interest, where eligibility or supporting documentation fails. The applicable amount and consequences depend on the facts, culpability, and procedural rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Deutsche Bundesbank (German Central Bank), in association with the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) for banking conduct and prudential supervision and the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK) for administration of the Foreign Trade and Payments Ordinance (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung – AWV).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Germany maintains fully liberalized current and capital account convertibility within the EU Treaty freedoms of payment and capital movement. The euro is fully convertible; there are no exchange control permissions, surrender mandates, or administrative ceilings on profit remittance, dividend distributions, or withdrawal of contributed capital. Nevertheless, the AWV imposes a mandatory cross-border payments statistical declaration to Deutsche Bundesbank for every resident payment to or receipt from a non-resident exceeding EUR 12,500. Dividend/profit remittance from a German UG is subject only to standard withholding tax (25% KapErtSt plus solidarity surcharge and, where applicable, church tax) or, for treaty/EU tax-exempt shareholders, zero withholding under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; no central bank approval or exchange allocation is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Germany has no forced export proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion into EUR, and no prescribed holding period for foreign-currency receivables. Export receipts may be retained in the original currency or charged out freely. The statutory obligation is purely statistical: under AWV Section 67, a resident recipient must report receipt of payment from a non-resident exceeding EUR 12,500 to Deutsche Bundesbank no later than the fifth working day after the day of receipt, stating the means of payment, counterparty, amount, currency, and purpose code. For bulk dried goji berry exports, the underlying commercial invoice, customs export declaration (ATLAS/Exit Summary Declaration), and transport documents constitute the evidential base for the Bundesbank report.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational settlement account and optional sub-account for escrow/capital reserves
Corporate operational account; commercial letter-of-credit and documentary collection rails
Operational treasury account, escrow-capable account, and trade-finance facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for non-EU offshore digital electronic-money institutions; MODERATE for EEA-licensed EMI/PI passporting into Germany under PSD2. Legal constraints: any payment account provider must hold a valid BaFin banking license or an EEA passport with notification under the German Payment Services Supervision Act (ZAG). Offshore EMIs from third countries cannot lawfully provide payment accounts or execute settlements for a German resident without a BaFin license/passport and will trigger correspondent-bank de-risking. EU-licensed EMIs are viable only for ancillary pre-funded treasury flows, not as the primary settlement account, because they are not licensed to grant credit, handle documentary credits, or accept term deposits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an Unternehmergesellschaft (haftungsbeschränkt) UG with a managing director, tier-one German banks ordinarily require a physical identification session of each managing director and signatory under the anti-money-laundering identification rules of Section 11 GwG; the Geldwäschegesetz allows video identification where the technical standard (videoIdent) is certified, and remote opening may be accepted by some banks for simple structures. In practice, for an onshore organic dried botanical exporter with a corporate name and cross-border clientele, the bank will require the managing director or an authorized agent to attend an on-site onboarding/integrity interview at the German branch, to present original passport/ID, proof of entitlement to represent the UG (commercial register excerpt), and to confirm the intended transaction profile. A purely offshore/digital opening without any physical nexus in Germany is not viable; a remote KYC flow can be used only if the bank explicitly approves electronic identification and the UG has a German registered office and telephone/address verifiability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: UG structure with a limited-liability class lacking minimum capital (EUR 1 nominal) and potentially minimal paid-in capital, raising shell-risk concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) current commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) evidencing valid incorporation and registered office; (ii) articles of association (Satzung) with shareholding table; (iii) Transparenzregister beneficial-ownership disclosure certificate; (iv) bank statement of paid-in capital and source-of-funds evidence; (v) last annual financial statements or a start-up balance sheet accompanied by auditor/accountant certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: cross-border trade in herbal botanicals/dried lycium may be classified as foodstuff/OS+/sensitive-agricultural product requiring statutory import/export licenses and phytosanitary inspection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) Gewerbeanmeldung commercial registration; (ii) German customs EORI number confirmation; (iii) EU/DE import/export license or organic-control body certificate (Öko-Kontrollstelle); (iv) phytosanitary certificate for botanical consignments; (v) food business operator notification under food hygiene law (LFGB); (vi) HACCP compliance statement; (vii) detailed product safety data sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident direct or indirect beneficiaries in certain jurisdictions elevate CDD to EDD and trigger refusal if ultimate ownership is not transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) complete corporate-chart evidence up to ultimate natural persons; (ii) official passports/tax identification numbers of UBOs; (iii) background/positive-news profile for each UBO; (iv) source of wealth / net worth statement; (v) tax residency certificates; (vi) declaration that no bearer shares or nominee arrangements exist; (vii) any existing bank reference letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: expected settlement flows from emerging-market/wholesale counterparties via third-country intermediary banks are not predictable or are inconsistent with stated wholesale activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) signed sale/purchase contracts and pro-forma invoices with defined payment terms; (ii) counterparty KYC passport and trade-register excerpt of each customer/supplier; (iii) due-diligence questionnaire with beneficial-ownership information for all counterparties; (iv) historical/godown logistics evidence and bills of lading for dried goji berry shipments; (v) a written treasury-liquidity forecast with expected MT103 references and country corridor rationale; (vi) sanctions/embargo screening confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a German UG, inbound shareholder equity injection must be routed to the German operational treasury account via SWIFT MT103/MT202 covering message using the IBAN starting with DE and the bank BIC. Wire instruction must bear a clear purpose text, e.g. 'Kapitaleinlage / Stammeinlage in die UG' or 'equity contribution', must not reference goods/services, and must be supported in bank records by (i) notarised share subscription/resolution (Übernahmevertrag), (ii) bank-book confirmation of contribution, and (iii) registration-ready declaration to the commercial register. Where the shareholder is a non-resident, the inward payment creates a statistical declaration obligation to Deutsche Bundesbank under AWV if the amount exceeds EUR 12,500; the German receiving bank may require the customer to complete the AWV cross-border receipt report. There is no approval requirement for the contribution, but the funds must be credited to an account in the UG's own name and may not be intermingled with trade settlement; a dedicated capital reserve sub-account is recommended.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for procurement and trade payables should be executed over clear electronic banking channels with SWIFT MT103 customer-credit transfers; high-value or documented-basis consignments should use irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit subject to UCP600, negotiated through the German relationship bank's trade-finance desk. For each disbursement above EUR 12,500 to a non-resident, the German resident must ensure the bank submits the AWV cross-border payment report to Deutsche Bundesbank. The instruction field must describe the underlying transaction (e.g. 'Payment for dried organic goji berry goods, invoice AB-1234') and include reference numbers, commodity description, currency, and beneficiary account. No third-party cash clearing or crypto-enabled settlement is permitted for formal UG trade disbursements; all payments must net through the banked treasury accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (outright delivery forwards) concluded with a licensed German/EU credit institution solely for hedging underlying euro/non-euro receivables or payables arising from goji berry trade
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with a BaFin-licensed counterparty for exotic-currency settlement corridors, limited to commodity trade hedging and limited to underlying trade exposure
Direct FX conversion on spot market via bank treasury windows
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) strictly for liquidity/term-matching of cash flows and not for speculative revenue enhancement
Participation in currency options with zero-premium structures, only to the extent permitted by the UG's finance policy and confirmed by the bank as eligible for hedge accounting treatment

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: UG statutory reserve appropriation (25% of annual net profit until share capital and reserves reach EUR 25,000)
stage_5.receiving_authority: None (corporate resolution by shareholders; no government filing)
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual financial statements are filed; with the balance-sheet date annual shareholders' meeting
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Non-observance makes the profit distribution unlawful; managing directors are personally liable for repayment; no strike-off.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15.825% (15% Körperschaftsteuer plus 0.825% solidarity surcharge); municipal trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) separately at 7%–17% depending on Hebesatz, producing a combined effective corporate burden of approximately 29%–33%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays or preferential rate for herbal wholesale. Ordinary business expenses are deductible; trade tax is deductible as an operating expense for corporate income tax purposes; export VAT is generally zero-rated for international bulk supply, but this does not reduce corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Körperschaftsteuererklärung (KSt-Erklärung) – Forms KSt 1 F (general information) and KSt 1 (taxable income); mandatory electronic filing through ELSTER or certified ERP/tax preparation software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 July of the calendar year following the tax year; automatically extended to 28/29 February of the second following year when the return is prepared and transmitted by a German tax advisor (Steuerberater).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered seat, civil law form (UG haftungsbeschränkt), Amtsgericht registry number, Steuernummer and tax office identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident sole shareholder must state foreign residential address and, where treaty relief is sought, provide tax residence certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Precise description and statistical classification of the commercial activity: international wholesale of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals (ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the German commercial activity accurately; do not claim a permanent establishment outside Germany unless actual fixed place of business and binding management functions exist in Germany.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start from commercial annual net income, then adjust for non-deductible expense additions and tax-exempt income deductions under §§ 7–10 KStG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure intercompany payments to non-resident affiliates are arm's length; excessive management fees or non-substantive royalty payments will be disallowed and reclassified as hidden profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 34 – Withholding tax credits and foreign taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim taxes paid abroad as credit under applicable double tax treaty if such taxes relate to German taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The UG cannot credit shareholder-level foreign tax on future dividends; shareholder-level withholding tax relief is claimed by the shareholder in cross-border repatriation procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the loss carryforward and carryback amounts applied to the current tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Preserve ownership and traceability of the UG's historical operating losses; a change of control above 25% or 50% may trigger loss forfeiture under § 8c KStG, directly impacting non-resident purchasing structures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty (Verspätungszuschlag) under § 152 AO: 0.25% of assessed tax for each commenced month, minimum €25, maximum €25,000; late payment surcharge under § 240 AO: 1% per month; administrative default assessments and enforcement surcharges may also apply; deliberate false filing constitutes criminal tax evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gewerbesteuererklärung (trade tax return) – Form GewSt 1 A via ELSTER; required because a UG carrying on commercial wholesale activity is subject to municipal trade tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory filing timeline as the corporate income tax return: 31 July of the following year, extended to 28/29 February of the second following year for tax-advisor-prepared returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of taxable income derived from the commercial operation before trade tax expense and after statutory addbacks and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must understand that trade tax attaches to German commercial activity regardless of the shareholder's place of residence; a mere holding shareholder with no German activity cannot file this return on behalf of the UG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For single-company entities, deductions are generally not required except in the case of taxable allocations from partnerships or other German collective enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the UG participates in a non-resident partnership selling dried goji berries into Germany, verify allocation rules under § 9 GewStG and treaty provisions to prevent double taxation of trade earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 30 – Taxable trade income after allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final trade tax assessment base after the €24,500 basic allowance (for sole traders/partnerships) and other statutory exemptions; corporations receive no basic allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the UG is a corporation, no trade tax allowance exists; the entire commercial profit is generally subject to municipal trade tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission and late payment penalties mirror the corporate income tax regime: late filing penalty up to €25,000, monthly late payment surcharge of 1%, plus local enforcement fees; incorrect declarations can trigger penalty assessments and criminal liability under § 370 AO.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 26.375% (25% capital gains/dividend withholding tax plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge on the withholding tax); treaty relief commonly reduces the rate to 15% or 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders; a full or 95% exemption may arise under § 8b KStG only where the receiving shareholder is a German corporation in specific intra-group structures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced dividend withholding tax under a double tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a valid tax residence certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) from the residence jurisdiction; (ii) submit the certificate and a shareholder analysis to the German paying entity before distribution, or to the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) in due time; (iii) use the BZSt relief-from-withholding or refund application; (iv) satisfy the beneficial-ownership and substance requirements of § 50d(3) EStG; and (v) maintain the shares with full enjoyment rights to distributions, profits, and liquidation proceeds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax of 15% plus solidarity surcharge, aggregate 15.825%, under § 50a EStG; treaty rates may reduce or eliminate this tax, typically 0%–10% depending on the IP type and treaty partner. Interest: ordinary arm's length cross-border interest is generally not subject to German withholding tax; profit-taking loans and silent partnership claims may be taxed as dividends or royalties and treaty rates then apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is required for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding EUR 5,000,000 for goods and EUR 500,000 for services in the relevant fiscal year; Master File documentation is required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue above EUR 100,000,000; Country-by-Country reporting applies where the group has consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Germany does not impose a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation; however, German tax authorities apply a robust substance-over-form doctrine, § 42 AO abuse-of-rights rules, the OECD Principal Purpose Test through the Multilateral Instrument, and § 50d(3) EStG beneficial-ownership requirements. A UG exporting dried goji berries must maintain a real German office, local employees, board decision-making power, contractual risk management, and actual economic activities; otherwise treaty benefits can be denied and income may be reallocated to the non-resident parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional submission of materially false corporate income tax, trade tax, or VAT returns; omission of export revenues; fabrication of supplier invoices; hidden bank accounts; use of untraceable cash transactions for commercial sales of dried goji berries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years or a statutory fine; especially serious cases carry imprisonment of 6 months to 10 years; tax understatements are collected with 6% annual late interest; property can be seized; limitation period extends to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors are jointly and severally liable under §§ 69, 71 AO and in practice may face attachment of personal assets, removal from office, travel bans, and imprisonment; civil restitution to the UG and creditors can additionally be ordered under § 823 BGB.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: UG registered with a mail-box address, no operating office, no employees, no demonstrated purchasing, warehousing, quality-control, or export-management functions; nominee directors and bank account arrangements; non-resident owner controls all substantive decisions outside Germany.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax treatment as a sham under § 41 AO and § 42 AO; the arrangement is disregarded and taxable income is reattributed to the true economic owner; treaty relief is denied under the Principal Purpose Test; 6% annual late interest and penalty assessments apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for defensive tax assessments, revocation of German residence permits, confiscation of assets, and criminal liability for facilitating tax evasion; cancellation of residency or entry bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sales of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals to a non-resident related distributor at prices below market without economic justification; failure to prepare Local File, Master File, or contemporaneous benchmarking; allocation of group profit to the UG while all functions, assets, and risks stay abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income is re-estimated under § 162 AO; transfer pricing documentation penalties of 5%–10% of the adjustment amount can be imposed up to a maximum, in addition to the underlying tax; administrative fines and late payment interest apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes caused by the transfer pricing adjustment; misleading or unavailable documentation exposes them to criminal fines and, where tax evasion is proven, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the UG as an invoicing vehicle to collect proceeds from unregulated sale of counterfeit or undeclared botanical goods; structuring cash or wire payments to avoid documentation thresholds; accepting known criminal proceeds through the corporate bank account; failing to maintain beneficial-owner identification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under § 261 StGB; imprisonment up to 5 years, in aggravated cases up to 10 years; confiscation of corporate assets; banking license and account terminations; administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or more for institutional failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face direct criminal liability, personal monetary fines, travel bans, and seizure of personal property; if the UG is used as a façade for laundering, courts may disregard limited liability and hold directors personally liable for all corporate funds involved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unauthorized import/export of dried goji berries or herbal botanicals without required German/EU customs declarations, food-safety licenses, phytosanitary certificates, or novel-food approvals; false commodity codes; undervaluation of export invoices to shift profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Seizure of goods, revocation of licenses, customs fines, re-assessment of customs duties and VAT, and possible ban on future exports; unlawful customs declarations may be prosecuted as fiscal fraud with imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false customs declarations are personally responsible, face structural liability to customs authorities, and can suffer travel restrictions, financial asset seizure, and imprisonment; the corporate veil will not protect deliberate wrongdoing.
